check.name: lens.design
check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

message.text: `#merged` treats a finding as dismissed only when no counted round holds it live (line 241 removes it from `dismissed` if any round has it live). Each round reads dismissals for itself, and a shared dismissal holds only for a round at the revision it was made at. `dismissalsOf` always tests the round being read (`[round, ...since]`), so a round of another revision always reads the dismissal as ended. The dismissal has one slot per finding: its key is the finding ID, and `ReviewRecords.made` makes each new dismissal supersede the ones standing. That slot holds exactly one revision. Pooling needs a dismissal that holds at every counted revision that raised the finding, and the slot cannot give one.

evidence.snippet:
- Any standing dismissal of a finding dismisses it, and each one's reason is shown.
- `melian dismiss` on a finding already dismissed adds a record that supersedes the dismissals it listed, so the new reason replaces the old and the superseded records are its history, as [the dismissal decision](2026-10-04-dismissal.md) rules. The same dismisser giving the same reason again adds nothing. Two dismissals stand together only when two writers dismissed at once.

- An unresolved acknowledge finding fails the gate, as a blocking finding does and as [the acknowledge status rule](2026-10-17-acknowledge-status-exact-rule.md) has it for a host's publication. A writer resolves one by recording the read as a dismissal with its reason, from any host, since a dismissal now reaches the record. [The Actions round's status](2026-11-07-actions-round-sets-melian-review.md) exempted an Actions round because a runner could not dismiss; that reason is gone, and so is the exemption once the gate is the required check. The maintainer ruled so on 2026-11-13, in the coordinator's session. Until then the Actions status keeps its own rule, as a display.

A shared dismissal holds only for a round at the revision it was made at. It ends once any round has been written at another revision, which the record's `frontier` lets the reader see. The reader needs no hunks from another revision, no git and no memory.

The guarantee: the reader never keeps a dismissal that any host would reopen. The cost the maintainer accepted: a push after a dismissal leaves the finding live in shared reads until someone dismisses it again.

The maintainer chose on 2026-11-20 that a shared dismissal holds only at the revision it was made at, and ends once any round is written at another revision. A revision is a base and a head. So a round of the same head at another base, a stacked parent's included, ends a dismissal made on the merge's own round when it is written later, even if it found nothing. The finding is then live, and the gate asks for the dismissal again. That fails closed. The gate's message names the round that ended the dismissal and the revision it reviewed, so a maintainer can see why a dismissed finding came back.

The gate asks again only for a finding its verdict holds live, and names each such dismissal once.

explanation.whatToDo: Decide dismissal at the gate once, against the merge's own revision, rather than per round. For example, take the dismissed set from the merge's own rounds (`own`). For rounds of another revision, count a finding as dismissed when a dismissal that holds at the merge revision covers it. Another option is to let a counted other-revision round accept a dismissal made at the merge revision when that round is in the dismissal's frontier. At minimum, do not print a `melian dismiss` remedy that cannot clear the finding. Instead, say that only a push or a new round clears it, and record that in the decision.
explanation.whyHere: The pooling decision exists because worst-of 'blocks its head for good'. It promises that an ended dismissal is answered by dismissing again, and gate.ts prints that remedy ('To dismiss it at this head: melian dismiss ...'). Base rule 7 says any standing dismissal of a finding dismisses it. Base rule 9 says a writer resolves an acknowledgement by recording a dismissal. The 2026-11-20 decision accepted a finding staying live only 'until someone dismisses it again'. Under pooling, dismissing again can never work for a finding that a counted round of another base raised on the merge's diff. The head stays blocked until a new push, which is the one-way door this change set out to remove. The head decision's own text says the other-base round ends the dismissal 'when it is written later', but the code ends it whatever the order, because the round being read always counts as moved.

properties.failureScenario:
Stacked PR #N at head H. Round P reviewed older..H, where older is an ancestor of the base tip, and raised P1 F in src/a.ts, a file on the merge's diff. Round R reviewed M..H, the merge's own revision, and raised F too. A maintainer runs `melian dismiss "#N" F --records git:melian/state`. The record's sighting.revision is M..H and its frontier is {P, R}.

At the gate, reading R: since=[R], every round is at M..H, so the dismissal holds and F is dismissed. Reading P: `moved = [P, ...]` finds that P.revision ≠ M..H, so the dismissal is `ended` and F is live in P's verdict. `#merged` line 241 deletes F from `dismissed` because P holds it live. The gate exits 1 and prints 'finding F is live ... To dismiss it at this head: melian dismiss "#N" F ...'.

Running that command writes a new dismissal that again names M..H and supersedes the old one. P reads it as ended again, and the gate exits 1 again, with no end. No dismissal at any single revision can hold for both P and R, because the one slot per finding takes one revision and each new dismiss supersedes the last. The test 'keeps a finding live when one counted round holds its dismissal and another, at another base, does not' pins this result, with P written before the dismissal. Outcome: the head can never pass the gate without a new push, and the gate's printed remedy misleads.
